# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 24 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 24 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_024_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 4, Chapter 3

**1** I asked her about the four colors the beast had on its head. She answered and said to me: "Again you are eager about such matters." "Yes, lady," I said, "tell me what they are." **2** "The black is this world in which you dwell. **3** The fiery and blood-red signifies that this world must be destroyed by blood and fire. **4** The golden part — you and all who flee from this world. For just as gold is refined by fire and becomes useful, so also you who dwell in it are being refined. Those therefore who remain and pass through the flames will be purified by them. Just as gold casts off its dross, so you also will cast off all grief and anguish, and will be purified and useful for the building of the tower. **5** The white part is the age to come, in which the elect of God will dwell. For those who are chosen by God will be spotless and pure, and the life of the coming age will be bright. **6** Therefore do not cease speaking in the ears of the saints; you have also the foreshadowing of the great tribulation to come. But if you are willing, it will be nothing. Remember those things which have been written before." **7** After she had said these things she departed, and I did not see in which direction she went, for there was a noise; and I turned back in fear, thinking that the beast was coming.

---

*EMET note: Vision 4.3 — the interpretation of the four colors: black = this world, blood-fire = its destruction, gold = the tested elect, white = the age to come. This is explicit eschatological schema.*
